searchText: +1 to moving to Monday from our side. +1 from my side as well Nethermind is ok with either. We just want to be 0-day ready for testnet. Note about the rayonism office hour tomorrow: it's scheduled for 9am UTC, and merge summit starts at 15:30 UTC. However, I was given different presentation times before, so I am not 100% yet on conflicts between the call or not. Update on client integration into local testnet tutorial: - Lighthouse PR merged (credits to <@!361447803194441738> ) - Nethermind PR merged (credits to <@!628018527470616606> ) - Nethermind Windows PR in review. Difficult to keep all client instructions windows-ified, it's probably better to use docker for non-nethermind clients. - Prysm PR ready (credits to <@!311971895828283393> <@!363800010518822915> ), waiting for SSZ nested-list tweak for compatible consensus between Prysm and other Eth2 clients. - Teku has docker instructions Tomorrow, after the Merge summit, I'll focus on test-running all clients, and preparing a deployment for the 1-day testnet next week. We'll run the majority of the validators on the network on a stable deployment, split between all participating eth2 validator client types, so we can ensure there are nodes online to test against. We will share enough keys so everyone can test block-proposals, but not to break finality when going offline or when repeatedly restarting during testing. I do not expect all participants will be online all the time, but coordinating around genesis would be nice. Monday for genesis is probably too early, Tuesday can work (assuming participants can start a node or two on Monday, and connect to the main deployment/bootnodes). I have a Nimbus branch aimed at this, but am not sure I'm testing it with the correct Catalyst branch -- is https://github.com/gballet/go-ethereum/tree/catalyst-for-rayonism/eth correct? catalyst has been merged into geth, you can now use `master` oh okay, and it has `consensus_newBlock` etc yes <@!654267572107083777> the tutorial-repo has some docs to get you started with catalyst and the whole testnet setup really: https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/ <@!203220829473996800> oh that answers a lot of questions, yeah. I had just been launching and syncing geth with `--goerli` basically It probably make sense to test deposit contract in this first short lived devnet to be able to make a fix if needed before the longer devnet launches FYI, I've tested Teku+Catalyst running from docker on a single Linux machine. Results: - `mkalinin/teku:rayonism` image has been updated - PR with fixes in instructions submitted, https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/pull/10 With this fixes and new image everything works fine <@!203220829473996800> about Windows PR - sure it was just a side-effect that someone might find useful. I wanted to run native so it happened. I will try WSL on the weekend - that could use mostly linux tutorial No problem <@!628018527470616606> , it was a good PR. But yes, docker or WSL can help Windows users run the linux instructions, and avoids the problem of out-of-date Windows instructions when all clients keep updating the linux side. Quick question, are we expecting 1559 to be part of rayonism dev nets? <dannyryan> no, execution layer should be built off of berlin Right, everything up to and including Berlin. We can look at EIP 1559 after Rayonism, it will be part of the eventual Merge (London before Merge). <dannyryan> similarly, beacon chain is based on phase 0 (rather than wip Altair). Easiest to build on what is supported in mainnet currently, will iterate specs once london and altair are production ready thanks for the clarification. We are hoping to have besu in the next dev net. Monday is probably too ambitious for us right now

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
Update on client integration into local testnet tutorial:
- Lighthouse PR merged (credits to <@!361447803194441738> )
- Nethermind PR merged (credits to <@!628018527470616606> )
- Nethermind Windows PR in review. Difficult to keep all client instructions windows-ified, it's probably better to use docker for non-nethermind clients.
- Prysm PR ready (credits to <@!311971895828283393> <@!363800010518822915> ), waiting for SSZ nested-list tweak for compatible consensus between Prysm and other Eth2 clients.
- Teku has docker instructions

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
Tomorrow, after the Merge summit, I'll focus on test-running all clients, and preparing a deployment for the 1-day testnet next week.

We'll run the majority of the validators on the network on a stable deployment, split between all participating eth2 validator client types, so we can ensure there are nodes online to test against. We will share enough keys so everyone can test block-proposals, but not to break finality when going offline or when repeatedly restarting during testing. I do not expect all participants will be online all the time, but coordinating around genesis would be nice. Monday for genesis is probably too early, Tuesday can work (assuming participants can start a node or two on Monday, and connect to the main deployment/bootnodes).
